sci-general-science-major.notes: Page defines no fixed course list: General Science requires 30 credits of Science courses numbered 300+ distributed across five designated subject areas, via Route A or Route B (student picks one route). Categories 1-2 are Route A; categories 3-5 are Route B. They are alternatives, not cumulative - total_credits 30 counts one route only. Each category's options are the five subject areas encoded as level_credit rules (min_level 300); the same area may not be reused across categories within a route (page requires distinct areas). Areas: Chemistry (CHEM 0081), Earth Science (ERSC 0225), Life Science (LFSC 0440), Mathematical Science (MASC 0029), Physics and Astronomy (PHYS 0271) - those parenthesized codes are internal area codes, not courses. Life Science PSYC eligibility (line 10: 'PSYC_V 348, 448 and PSYC_V courses numbered 60 to 89 in the last two digits') is now enumerated exactly as include_courses against valid_codes.txt at the 300/400 level: PSYC 348, 361, 363, 365, 367, 368, 370, 371, 388, 448, 460, 461, 462, 472, 488. PSYC is NOT in include_subjects, so no other PSYC course counts. EOSC 471 appears in the Earth Science exclusion list but not in the Life Science inclusion list, so it counts toward neither area. GEOB is the legacy code for GEOS; GEOB 307/407 are page synonyms but GEOB codes are not in valid_codes.txt (GEOS 307/407 are). Codes MRNE, PCTH, MEDG, CAPS, ATSC verified present in valid_codes.txt. Additional page rules not encoded as categories: at most 3 credits of directed studies inside the 30 upper-level credits, at most 6 credits of directed studies in the whole degree; courses must be acceptable for major/honours options in the area; Route A records areas of concentration on the transcript. First- and second-year requirements defer to faculty-wide Lower-Level Requirements and Promotion Requirements (out of scope).

sci-pharmacology-honours.notes: Honours (0019) Pharmacology (PCTH), source lines 93-179. Printed year totals: First 31 (line 114), Second 34 (line 135), Third+Fourth 67 (line 164), degree 132 (line 166) — these four are mutually consistent (31+34+67=132), so the totals column is treated as authoritative where individual cells conflict with it. TWO source cells do not reconcile with the printed year totals and have been corrected: (a) 'CHEM_V 205 or CHEM_V 211' prints 4 credits (line 124-125), but with 4 the Second Year line items sum to 35 vs the printed 34; the Major's identical row prints 3 (line 42-43), CHEM 205 is a 3-credit course, and footnote 9 ('students who take CHEM 211 reduce electives by 1') only makes sense against a 3-credit baseline — encoded at 3. (b) Third/Fourth 'Electives' prints 19 (line 161-162), but the twelve required non-elective rows in that section sum to 45 (3+3+3+6+3+3+3+3+6+6+3+3), so electives must be 22 to reach the printed 67 — encoded at 22. With both corrections the encoded categories sum to 28 (First) + 34 (Second) + 67 (Third/Fourth) = 129; the first-year 'Additional Communication Requirement' (3 cr, line 97-98) is the faculty-wide Communication Requirement and is deliberately not encoded, so 129 + 3 = 132 = the stated degree total. Confidence is medium rather than high solely because two printed cells had to be overridden to reconcile. Elective blocks encoded with empty options to preserve credit accounting. kin-neuromechanical-physiological-scienc.notes: Source: https://vancouver.calendar.ubc.ca/faculties-colleges-and-schools/school-kinesiology/bachelor-kinesiology/neuromechanical-and-physiological-sciences. Page gives a year-by-year credit table (30+30+60=120) plus two trailing prose rules. All courses are 3 credits per the table. Code verification against valid_codes.txt: every named course exists EXCEPT KIN 420 (appears in the 'Select 7 from' list but is NOT in valid_codes.txt) — recorded anyway. Ambiguity: the 'Select 7 from ...' 21-credit row and the trailing 'at least 21 credits from those listed below' rule almost certainly describe the same 21 credits, but the two course lists differ (the trailing lists add KIN 310, 324, 330, 421, 423, 428; the Select-7 list adds KIN 420), so both are encoded and a planner should treat them as overlapping, not additive. Similarly the 'minimum 36 credits of 300/400-level KIN' rule overlaps the Select-7 (21) + KIN Electives (15) rows = 36, and the year 3/4 'Electives 1,3' row carries conflicting footnotes (1 = any KIN or non-KIN elective; 3 = KIN 300/400-level), so it is encoded as unrestricted with the conflict noted. Generic elective rows are included for credit accounting with empty options. Footnote 2: students interested in KIN 342, 442, 444 should take KIN 140 as a year 1 or 2 elective (advisory, not encoded as a category).
